verdict: Western Digital's revenue jumped 55% to $4.4B and profit hit $1.8B as AI data centers bought high-capacity disk drives at sharply higher prices.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $3.07 a year ago; non-GAAP EPS was $4.64

segments.name: Cloud
segments.note: Hard drives for data centers and big enterprise customers — 88% of all revenue. Exabytes shipped rose more than 20% and the average price per exabyte rose about 25% on AI-driven demand.

segments.name: Client
segments.note: Drives sold into PCs and other devices through computer makers and distributors — more than doubled off a small base.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.note: Retail external drives and other consumer products — prices per exabyte rose about 70% while units shipped fell about 30%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing higher-capacity drive technology — actually down from $294M a year ago.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the drives and running the company.

opex.name: Business realignment charges
opex.note: Restructuring charges — severance and related costs of reshaping the business.

otherDetail: Interest and other expense of $8M, net.
oneTimers: $43M of business realignment (restructuring) charges are inside operating expenses. Excluding them and similar adjustments, non-GAAP EPS was $4.64 versus GAAP EPS of $4.63 — a nearly clean quarter.
footerNote: End-market revenue (Cloud, Client, Consumer) is the disaggregation in the Form 10-Q; the earnings release reports the same income-statement totals.

takeaways.title: It is a cloud company now
takeaways.text: Cloud was $3,868M of the $4,381M total, up 54% — data centers racing to store AI data bought more exabytes at about 25% higher prices per exabyte.

takeaways.title: Pricing power showed up in margin
takeaways.text: Gross margin jumped to 57.8% from 43.5% a year ago, and operating margin reached 46.7% — scarce high-capacity drives are being sold at premium prices.

takeaways.title: Guidance says more of the same
takeaways.text: For FY27 Q2 Western Digital guided to revenue of about $5.1B (up 66–72% YoY) and non-GAAP gross margin around 60.5% — and raised the quarterly dividend 17% to $0.175 a share.
